title: Lincoln City vs. Wrexham: Preview, Predictions and Lineups
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Rich FayNov 20, 2026Wrexham celebrated League One promotion the last time they faced Lincoln City. / Justin Setterfield/Getty Images (Lincoln), Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty Images (Wrexham)Wrexham return to Championship action this weekend when they travel to face Lincoln City at Sincil Bank.

The Red Dragons entered the November international break on a high after beating Middlesbrough and drawing with Wolves. They will now look to climb the Championship table during a packed festive fixture schedule.

Phil Parkinson’s side won’t face a team currently in the top 10 in any of their next six matches, with four of those opponents sitting below them in the table. Lincoln are 21st, having lost their last three matches in a row, but have produced some impressive results this season.

Lewis O’Brien has been brilliant in the solitary attacking midfield role across the previous two matches. / Malcolm Couzens/Getty ImagesWrexham hope to make serious progress over the next few weeks as they face teams below them in the Championship. The Red Dragons have developed a reputation for coming good during the winter months and grinding out results during the most demanding period of the season.
This weekend will mark Wrexham’s first trip to Lincoln since they celebrated promotion from League One two years ago with a victory on the final day of the season.

Lincoln could keep their back three defense to combat Wrexham. / FotMobLincoln City will have to make at least one change against Wrexham this weekend, with Conor McGrandles suspended. The Imps have switched to a three-man defense in their last two matches and could look to match Wrexham’s tactical setup with the same approach.
Mikkel Ladefoged is one to watch, having scored three goals in just 318 minutes this season, while experienced defender Adam Reach is another key figure in their squad.
Lincoln City predicted lineup (3-4-2-1): Wickens; Elerewe, Jefferies, Bradley; Oyegoke, Konak, Bayliss, Reach; Hackett-Fairchild, Draper, Ladefoged.

Wrexham are still without several attacking options. / FotMobWrexham could stick with the recent formation change that has helped them compensate for a lack of attacking options in recent weeks. Kieffer Moore should lead the line after his recent withdrawal from international duty, with Lewis O’Brien operating in the attacking midfield role.
Danny Imray could be handed a start at right wingback following Issa Kaboré’s withdrawal from the Burkina Faso squad, while Parkinson may opt to retain George Dobson in a three-man midfield.
Wrexham predicted lineup (3-5-1-1): Patterson; Cleworth, Worrall, Doyle; Imray, Whiteman, Dobson, Thomason, Ekomié; O’Brien; Moore.
